claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor resistance to oxygen attack.
Pack cementation aluminizing at approximately 1050 °C for 4 hours will induce a protective Al₂O₃ surface layer on cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminizing treatment will produce a thin, adherent alumina scale.
The resulting alumina coating will be continuous and nanometer-scale.
The alumina scale will act as a diffusion barrier to oxygen ingress during high-temperature exposure.
Impeding oxygen ingress will protect the alloy bulk from oxidation.
The surface treatment will leave the bulk microstructure largely unchanged.
Leaving the bulk microstructure unchanged will preserve the alloy's intrinsic mechanical properties.
Aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit lower oxidation weight gain than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr during exposure around 1000 °C for up to 24 hours.
Aluminized HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit less oxygen penetration than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr during high-temperature exposure.
The treated alloy will retain the untreated alloy's room-temperature tensile ductility.
The treated alloy will retain the untreated alloy's yield strength at 1000 °C over strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
Extensive thermal cycling or operation outside the stated temperature, atmosphere, duration, and strain-rate boundaries may alter coating performance.
